correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the geometry in hyperboloid coordinates: at a ridge the spatial transverse radius is s sin α, hence its circumference is 2πs sin α and its face has intrinsic radius ρ with sinh ρ=s sin α. The plane is X₃=(s/c)cos α X₀. The outward unit sphere and plane normals have dot product cos α/√(1+s²sin²α), giving exterior angle arctan(c tan α). The spherical belt has smooth mean curvature 2c/s, the disks zero, so the area and curvature split into the two claimed one-side contributions. A′<0 parameterizes the entire nearby fixed-total-area slice by x±h, with quadratic coefficient m″(x). In the shallow expansion the α² terms cancel and the numerator of the inverse second derivative first has coefficient 48(b₆a₄−b₄a₆)α⁷ in units of 2π; the α⁹ in the denominator yields the stated α⁻² law with its correct 2π factor. In u=cos α at the deep endpoint, A′=2πs² is nonzero; B″=−π²s and A″=−2πs²/c give the second stated limit. Independent representative coefficient-sign comparisons agree, but the endpoint expansions prove the sign intervals. The two critical radii are strictly ordered, the vanishing leading coefficients there are not assigned strict signs, and no unrestricted variation or global minimum is inferred.
